question: What is the main idea of the passage?

option.a: Intelligence is fixed at birth and cannot be changed.
option.b: Only a lucky few are born with the ability to learn.
option.c: Ability can develop through effort, strategy and good teaching.
option.d: Examinations are the best way to measure intelligence.

section:
Many people assume that intelligence is fixed at birth, but research in psychology suggests otherwise. The brain remains adaptable throughout life, a quality scientists call neuroplasticity. Whenever a learner acquires a new skill, fresh connections form between nerve cells, strengthening the networks that support memory and reasoning. This evidence challenges the old belief that only a lucky few are born clever. It suggests that consistent effort, curiosity and good study habits can shape achievement far more than natural talent alone.

Yet effort must be guided. A student who reads without reflecting, or who repeats the same exercise without seeking feedback, may work hard and still make little progress. Effective learning therefore requires both persistence and strategy: setting clear goals, testing one's understanding and correcting mistakes. Teachers also matter. When they explain ideas in different ways and encourage questions, they help learners build durable knowledge. Countries that invest in well-trained teachers and well-equipped classrooms often record better learning outcomes than those that rely on examination drills. The lesson is simple: ability can grow, but it grows best in an environment that rewards thoughtful effort and sound teaching.
solution: The passage argues that intelligence is not fixed and that effort, strategy and good teaching help ability grow. Option C captures this central idea.

question: Theatre was popular in Africa because__________

option.a: was traditional and simple in nature
option.b: dealt with the political, social, and economic problems of the society
option.d: was communal and reflected the common concerns of the people

section:
Theatre in the recent past used to be a very popular art in traditional African society. It used to be a point of intersection where members of the community not only come to entertain themselves, 'but join heads together'. In the traditional context of African drama, therefore, theatre was popular and respectable institution which preserved the people's culture and tradition. Theatre was popular with the people because it emphasized community participation, peace and progress. The presentations focused on the people's lives, their aspirations, fears, and hopes. But today, the situation is different. Theatre is becoming very unpopular.

Africa of the present age is pre-occupied with many problems yearning for immediate solutions. The continent is facing hydra-head challenges - challenges on the political, social, and economic scenes. In a world where Science and Technology are seen as the solutions to these problems, little attention is paid to the arts. Literature generally, and drama in particular is often rated very low on the utility-scale. Many Africa today look at drama and theatre as a mere thing of fun, a joke so to say.

Elitism is another barrier that militates against the appreciation of theatre as a communal art. Folk theatre is appreciated by a negligible number of people, contemporary focus is on literary theatre. Unfortunately, literary theatre only pretends to serve the interest of its society while in reality, it has a foreign audience in mind. The use of European and American theatrical conventions by our academic playwrights can bear witness to this anomaly.

The popularity of the literary African theatre is further marred by the medium of communication as most literary dramas in Africa are written in foreign languages which are not understood by many Africans. The question often asked is whether the artist should climb down to the level of his community of stay at his exalted height and wait for the community to gradually move up to him.
solution:
The correct answer is D — was communal and reflected the common concerns of the people.

In the passage, paragraph one emphasizes on community participation, peace and progress.

Theatre was popular with the people because it emphasized community participation, peace and progress. The presentations focused on the people's lives, their aspirations, fears, and hopes. But today, the situation is different. Theatre is becoming very unpopular.

Africa of the present age is pre-occupied with many problems yearning for immediate solutions. The continent is facing hydra-head challenges - challenges on the political, social, and economic scenes. In a world where Science and Technology are seen as the solutions to these problems, little attention is paid to the arts. Literature generally, and drama in particular is often rated very low on the utility-scale. Many Africa today look at drama and theatre as a mere thing of fun, a joke so to say.

Elitism is another barrier that militates against the appreciation of theatre as a communal art. Folk theatre is appreciated by a negligible number of people, contemporary focus is on literary theatre. Unfortunately, literary theatre only pretends to serve the interest of its society while in reality, it has a foreign audience in mind. The use of European and American theatrical conventions by our academic playwrights can bear witness to this anomaly.

The popularity of the literary African theatre is further marred by the medium of communication as most literary dramas in Africa are written in foreign languages which are not understood by many Africans. The question often asked is whether the artist should climb down to the level of his community of stay at his exalted height and wait for the community to gradually move up to him.
solution:
The correct answer is A — is regarded as not being of much use.

In the passage, paragraph 2 tells us drama is often rated as very low on the utility scale.

question: It is important for university to be independent so that they can________

option.c: be left to expand without any hindrances

section:
The financing of the university will always be a vexatious problem not only because of the need for it to maintain a level of independence that allows for the thriving of intellectual pursuit but also for the size of the funding that is required to maintain an acceptable level of infrastructure in a modern university. The experience of the Nigerian university in recent years has, in this regard, been almost alarming. The funding levels requited constitute sufficient reasons for diversifying the sources. Even if the government was in a position on its own to meet all of the university's financial requirements, I consider it desirable that every effort be made to reduce such contribution in the interest of university autonomy. I also hold the view that the university should seek to become dependent, in a substantial way, on funds generated from within. In other words, the sources of funding the university should be diversified as much as possible. Based on this principle, ·we can identify four sources - government, industry, students, and individual philanthropists. I must add quickly that each source has its own set of problems in its continuous interaction with the university, which ought to be addressed here.

Of all the four major sources of financing university education mentioned above, contribution through fees from the students involves intricate issues of special concern If government gives as an expression of its obligation to promote the general welfare of society if industry gives in order to enhance its chances of procurement of needed human information and material resources, as well as enhance its social responsibility if the general public gives as an indication of voluntary support for a worthy social cause, students (and by inference, their parents) should give in order to purchase an economic good for meeting their own felt need in the expectation that they will be satisfied with the product purchased.

[Adapted from Onosode, GO: 'The politics of Managing People, Prospects and Poverty: The Role of the University, 1990 OAU Convocation}
solution:
The correct answer is C — be left to expand without any hindrances.

In the passage, Paragraph one talks about the need for Universities to maintain a level of independence which enables Universities to thrive for intellectual pursuit. The writer also emphasizes the need for University autonomy. All these points out to the need to expand and function independently.

Mr Bello, Aliya's father, almost fainted when he heard the shocking news that some students had been caught on the school's basketball court late at night. As a caring parent, he was deeply upset by the report.

question: In the following options, lettered A to D, all the words except one have the same stress pattern. Choose the one with the different stress pattern.
section: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. The stressed syllable is written in capital letters.
solution:

COL-umn is stressed on the first syllable, so it has a different stress pattern. Option D is correct.

Calculator
section: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. The stressed syllable is written in capital letters.
solution:
The correct answer is A — CAL-cu-la-tor.

Calculator has its stress on its first syllable. For nouns, the stress is usually on the first syllable except if there is a weak vowel ( /ə/ or /ɪ/) on the first syllable, then it moves to the next one. Since calculator ( /ˈkæl.kjə.leɪ.tər/) does not have a weak vowel in the first syllable, the stress is placed there.

Criticism
section: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. The stressed syllable is written in capital letters.
solution:
The word is cri-ti-ci-sm. Many English nouns that end in -ism take their main stress on the first syllable, so we say CRI-ti-ci-sm.

Say it aloud and listen for the strongest beat: it comes first. That matches option D.

question:
From the words lettered A to D, choose the one that has the correct stress

Expenditure
section: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. The stressed syllable is written in capital letters.
solution:
The word ex-pen-di-ture has four syllables, and the main stress falls on the second one: ex-PEN-di-ture.

Words that end in -ture, such as departure and adventure, are usually stressed just before that ending, so option B is correct.

question: The man, as well as the woman ________ arrested
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — has been.

In the rule of concord, 'when words such as, as well as, alongside, together with, no less than etc are used, the verb that follows would be the same with the subject of the phrase or clause, that is, the noun or the pronoun that comes before the marker of accompaniment.

'The man' is a singular noun hence a singular verb is needed.

Note that 'arrested' can function as past tense or past participle but in this context, it is a past participle.

However, 'is' is a singular verb used in the present tense, 'has' is a singular used in the perfect tense, 'have' is a singular and plural verb used in the perfect tense and 'been' is used in the perfect tense.

Therefore, option B is the correct answer.

question: Many a ____________ to understand me
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — man fails.

In the rule of Concord, 'when many-a is used, the verb and the noun that follows must be singular'

question: It is you that __________ to write the letter
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is D — are supposed.

The law of proximity states that any subject closest to the verb element controls the verb form.

The sentence has a singular subject 'it' and a plural subject 'you', hence a plural verb is needed because 'you' is closer.

Similarly, 'supposed' is most appropriate because of the relative clause 'that'. This implies that supposed functions as an 'adjective' in this context which means 'intended'

Option D is the correct answer.

question: My father _______ on the floor
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is D — has lain.

'My Father' as the subject is in the third person category, should be followed by the auxiliary verb 'has'

Think of the verb 'lie' as a word with two different meaning.

The first 'lie' means 'to rest in a horizontal position' The following are its past, present participle or past participle tense respectively, (lay, lying , lain)

The second lie means 'to give false information' The following are its past, present participle or past participle tense respectively, (lied, lying, lied)

Contextually and grammatically option D is the correct answer.

question: This class __________students and teachers
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — comprises.

Comprise means 'made up of'. Therefore, to say 'Comprises of/ Comprise of ' is a tautology.

Note that, singular verbs must agree with a singular noun.

The subject of the sentence is 'This Class' which is a singular noun

This makes Option B correct.

question: Before I arrived, the choir _______ the hymn
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The sentence tells us about two past actions. I arrived (simple past) and the choir sang before that. The earlier action needs the past perfect tense, made with had + past participle.

The past participle of sing is sung, so we say the choir had sung the hymn. Option C is correct.

question: The soldier _________ his gun on the wall after the armed robber______
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
Two verbs are tested here: hang meaning to put something up, and hang meaning to kill someone by the neck.

For an object the past tense is hung (the soldier hung his gun on the wall). For an execution the past participle is hanged (the robbers had been hanged). Option B joins both correctly.

question: Thank you for the __________ of presenting my paper.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct spelling is privilege — p-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e. It has no extra d and no second e before the g.

A handy way to remember is privi + lege, with the same ending as college. Option C is correct.

question: My brother graduated from university last year; he will soon_________
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — convoke.

The appropriate verb to be used in this context is 'Convoke'

Note; the word 'Convocate' is archaic (no longer in use)

question: You need to __________your points
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct spelling is expatiate, which means to explain a point in great detail. We pronounce it ex-PA-ti-ate.

Many people wrongly add an n and write expantiate, but that spelling is not standard English. Option C is correct.

question: All the people in the bus died in that _________ accident
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
An accident in which all the people in the bus died is a fatal accident. Fatal means causing death.

The other words describe how bad or careless something is, but they do not carry the idea of death, so option C fits best.

question: All the ________ were stolen by the thieves
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct expression is arms and ammunition. Arms are weapons, and ammunition is the bullets or explosives used with them.

Ammunition is an uncountable noun, so it never takes an -s, while arms is always plural in this phrase. Option B is correct.

question: What a ________! the more you look, the less you see
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is D — paradox.

The more you look, the less you see is contradictory and that is a paradox.

question: The soldiers pledge their ________ loyalty to the new government
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — complete.

Option C best completes the sentence above. 'Complete' suggests 'entire or total'

After interrogation, the police ______ the information from the suspect.

For one who never tells you everything, 'Secrecy' best completes the sentence above.

question: __________ packages should always be handled with care

question: Because of the hard times, workers live in ___________ poverty

Parochial means having a limited or narrow scope. Option C best fits this definition.

question: I went through his work; it was gibberish

question: If he declines the offer, it will be better for him.

Decline means to refuse or say no to something. So if he declines the offer, he rejects it.

Ignore means to pay no attention, deny means to say something is untrue, and snub means to treat someone coldly. Option D is closest.

question: The appearance which the famous actor made last month was his swan song. This meant that_________

question: Muiz does not let the grass grow under his feet. This means that Muiz _________

option.a: does not waste time in doing things

question: A suitable title for the passage is
section:
Read the passages below and answer the questions that follow:

Everyone is tired or fatigued at some time. The major cycle in your life is work, fatigue and rest in that order. Fatigue is characteristic of your body. It does not occur in a man-made machine which operates as long as its parts are intact and it has fuel. But your body, a living machine, has a definite limitation - its work continues, it gradually loses its responsiveness, becomes less irritable, turns out less work and finally may not respond at all. The feeling of fatigue usually expresses itself in three ways: first, there is a feeling of tiredness and a marked desire for rest. Second, efficiency is greatly reduced. Third, there may be definite physiological changes in your body, low blood pressure, loss of muscle tone, tremors, and poor muscular coordination, and in other ways. Fatigue, however, may express itself in many ways for there are many different forms of it. The fatigue of a student. for example, who has worked all evening on a difficult lesson, is different from that of a labourer who has worked all day at a back-breaking task, or that of a business executive who worries with the stress and strain of organisation.
solution:
The passage explains what fatigue is, how it builds up in the body, and how rest helps us recover. Every paragraph keeps returning to that single idea.

A good title should cover the whole passage, and Fatigue does so in one word. The other options are too narrow or describe only a small detail.

nonentity: a person or thing with no special or interesting qualities; an unimportant person or thing.

question: The soldiers were remorseful for their inhuman treatment of the civilians.
section: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is A — boastful.

Remorseful: filled with remorse; sorry.

Boastful: showing excessive pride and self-satisfaction in one's achievements, possessions, or abilities.

question: Insecurity has escalated since the present government came into power.
section: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is A — abated.

Escalate: increase rapidly.

Abate: (of something unpleasant or severe) become less intense or widespread

question: He maintained that Nigerians need a leader with an iron fist
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is B — severe in treatment.

Iron fist is used in reference to the exercise of power in an oppressive or ruthless way. A particularly severe, forceful, and uncompromising manner of ruling/governing.

question: The emphasis placed on good moral conduct by the society in the past seems to have been relaxed
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
Relaxed here means made less strict or less firm. If the emphasis on good conduct has been relaxed, it has been weakened.

Option C, weakened, is nearest in meaning. It does not mean the conduct is completely outdated or avoided.

question: The matter was considered a private concern of the chairman to handle
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is A — personal.

Private: belonging to or for the use of one particular person or group of people only.

question: He was underrated at the preliminary stage of the competition
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is B — initial.

Preliminary: preceding or done in preparation for something fuller or more important.

question: The office assistant was dismissed for pilfering
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
Pilfering means stealing small things, often little by little. So the office assistant was dismissed for stealing.

The other options do not mean taking what does not belong to you, so option C is correct.

question: choose the option with the correct spelling from the options lettered A-E
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct spelling is interpret — i-n-t-e-r-p-r-e-t. It has no extra e at the end and no double t.

Remember the pattern inter + pret, as in interpretation. Option B is correct.

question: choose the option with the correct spelling from the options lettered A-E
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct spelling is successful — s-u-c-c-e-s-s-f-u-l. It begins with one s, then has double c, double s, and ends with a single l.

A helpful memory aid: success + ful = successful. Option C is correct.

question: choose the option with the correct spelling from the options lettered A-E
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct spelling is accommodation — a-c-c-o-m-m-o-d-a-t-i-o-n. It has double c and double m.

Think of it as "a + ccom + modation": two c's and two m's. Option D is correct.

question: The two friends made promises to _____ when they met last year
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
When two people do something to each other we use each other; for more than two we use one another.

The sentence says "The two friends", so each other is correct. Also, theirselves is not standard English; the correct word is themselves. Option A is correct.

question: The meeting was organised at _______ instance ?
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The gap needs the possessive form of who, which is whose. It tells us that the meeting was organised at the instance of whom.

Whose's and whom's are not correct English words, so option C is correct.

question: Mr. Jude made the meeting _____his poor health
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — in spite of.

"In spite of" means despite or regardless of. Other prepositions are not phrased correctly or cannot fill the gap.

question: The manager met the ______ who came visiting last week
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — good-looking tall dark American.

good-looking(opinion)

question: Head
section: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the underlined letter(s).

The letters ea in head are pronounced /e/, the short sound you hear in bed.

Red also has the /e/ sound, while bead and rear have /iː/ and stir has /ɜ/. Option B is correct.

question: Moon
section: Choose the word that has the same vowel sound as the underlined letter(s).

The letters oo in moon are pronounced /uː/, a long sound.

Loop also has the long /uː/, while cook, pull and look have the short /ʊ/. Option B is correct.

question: King

solution:
The word king ends with the sound /ŋ/, the "ng" sound made at the back of the mouth.

question: Teach
section: Choose the word that has the same consonant sound as the underlined letter(s).

Deviate ends with the /t/ sound (de-vi-ate). Through, wrath and both contain /θ/, and the t in listen is silent. Option A is correct.

question: Biography
section: Choose the option that best explains the implication of the emphatic stress in the sentence.

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2021.

He was not jailed for murder or smuggling, so option C is correct.

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2021.

The correct answer is A — First-person and Third person point of view.

The author mixes two points of view. The writer starts with the first person point of view and slides into the third person point of view.

question: What brand of Phone did Salim buy?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2021.
solution:
Salim bought a Samsung phone. The phone matters in the story because it later leads him into trouble on social media.

question: Omar's achievement was by no means a small feat. This means that?

option.c: Omar's achievement was not as difficult as it seems
option.d: His accomplishment was not by a small feat

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2021.

question: Habib gives Tomiwa a bundle of _______?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2021.

Habib gives Tomiwa a bundle of five hundred naira notes.

Tomiwa is Salma's roommate, and this gift forms part of the story of how the friends relate to one another. Option B is correct.

question: What did the author of the book study?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.

question: The book described Talle as a?

solution:

Ummi's husband hoped to study law, but life took a different turn and he ended up studying accounting.

IPO stands for Investigating Police Officer. This is the police officer who investigates a case and gathers facts about it.

question: What is Ummi's Occupation?

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.

EMEC means Examination Malpractice and Ethics Committee. It is the body in the novel that handles cases of cheating in examinations.

Notice the two key words: Malpractice and Ethics. Option A is correct.

question: What is the full name of Salma?

question: Who was the narrator of the life changer?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
The narrator of The Life Changer is Ummi. She tells the story herself, including memories of her youth and her children's experiences.

Because she narrates it, the story is told from her own point of view. Option B is correct.

question: How old is Bint ?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
Bint is five years old. She is the youngest child in Ummi's family and the baby of the house.

Her age explains her innocent and amusing questions. Option C is correct.

question: What question did Bint ask her teacher?

option.b: How to say what is your name
option.d: How to say that's very good

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.

Bint asked her teacher how to say "that's very good". She wanted to know the correct English expression to use when praising someone.

Her question shows how curious and eager to learn she is. Option D is correct.

question: Who were the people in the car?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.

The people in the car were Habib and Labaran. They are the young men whose car features in an important incident in the story.

The correct answer is D — Twenty Thousand naira.

This can be found in chapter 5 of the novel. Habib gave Tomiwa a total of fifty thousand naira. However, she was told to give each of her three roommates ten thousand naira while she can keep twenty thousand naira for herself.

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
The correct answer is B — Ten thousand Naira.

Tomiwa gave her roommates ten thousand naira each. Habib gave Tomiwa fifty thousand naira and was told to take twenty thousand for herself and to share the rest among her three roommates.

question: What was Omar's JAMB exam?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
Omar scored 230 in his JAMB examination. That score was good enough to earn him admission into the university.

His result is a proud moment for Ummi, who values education highly. Option A is correct.

question: What is the full meaning of the acronym EMAL
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
EMAL stands for Examination Malpractice. In the novel it is the offence of cheating or breaking examination rules.

This is different from EMEC, which is the committee that handles such cases. Option A is correct.

question: Who introduced the snail delicacy?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
The snail delicacy was introduced by Tomiwa. She is Salma's roommate and a friend of the other girls.

Tomiwa's snail dish becomes a talking point among the friends. Option D is correct.

question: "Nothing happened, My friend didn't feel like giving you her number so she gave you mine instead" Who is the friend?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
The "friend" in the statement is Salma. She says this to explain why she gave a young man her own phone number instead of her friend's.

The line shows Salma's bold, playful character. Option A is correct.

question: It might be said that there is some kind of sibling rivalry between
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
There is a kind of sibling rivalry between Teemah and Omar. They are brother and sister who often tease and compete with each other.

Their playful quarrels are part of the family life described in the novel. Option B is correct.

question: One reason the narrator had the habit of entering her children's room unannounced was because

option.a: to monitor their hygiene and tidiness
option.d: to keep them studying their books

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
The narrator entered her children's rooms unannounced to monitor their hygiene and tidiness. She wanted to make sure the rooms were clean and well kept.

She was not spying on them; she was checking their neatness. Option A is correct.

question: According to the story, one of the following is true

option.b: Ada and Salma are course mates

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Life Changer by Khadija Abubakar Jalli, the JAMB reading text for 2022.
solution:
The true statement is that Salma and Tomiwa are roommates. They share the same room at the university hostel.

That is why their friendship, and their quarrels, are so close and personal. Option D is correct.

question: Early in which month did the southwest monsoon break?
section:
May in Ayemenem is a hot, brooding month. The days are long and humid. The river shrinks and black crows gorge on bright mangoes in still, dust green trees. Red bananas ripen. Jackfruits burst. Dissolute blue bottles hum vacuously in the fruity air. Then they stun themselves against clear windowpanes and die, fatly baffled in the sun. The nights are clear but suffused with sloth and sullen expectations.

But by early June the southwest monsoon breaks and there are three months of wind and water with short spells of sharp, glittering sunshine that thrilled children snatch to play with. The countryside turns an immodest green. Boundaries blur as tapioca fences take root and bloom. Brick walls turn mossgreen. Pepper vines snake up electric poles. Wild creepers burst through laterite banks and spilt across the flooded roads. Boats ply in the bazaars. And small fish appear in the puddles that fill the PWD potholes on the highways. It was raining when Rahel came
back to Ayemenem.

Slanting silver ropes slammed into loose earth, ploughing it up like gunfire. The old house on the hill wore its steep, gabled roof pulled over its ears like a low hat. The walls, streaked with moss, had grown soft and bulged a little with dampness that seeped up from the ground. The wild, overgrown garden was full of the whisper and scurry of small lives.In the undergrowth, a rat snake rubbed itself against a glistening stone. Hopeful yellow bullfrogs cruised the scummy pond for mates. A drenched mongoose flashed across the leaf-strewn driveway. The house itself looked empty. The doors and windows were locked. The front verandah bare. Unfurnished.

But the sky blue Plymouth with chrome tail fins was still parked outside, and inside, Baby Kochamma was still alive. She was Rahel's baby grand aunt, her grandfather's younger sister. Her name was really Navomi, Navomi Ipe, but everybody called her Baby. She became Baby Kochamma when she was old enough to be an aunt. Rahel hadn't come to see her, though.
Neither niece nor baby grandaunt laboured under any illusions on that account. Rahel had come to see her brother, Estha. They were two-egg twins. "Dizygotic' doctors called them. Born from separate but simultaneously fertilized eggs. Estha Esthappen-was the older by 18 minutes.
solution:
The passage says that "by early June the southwest monsoon breaks". The monsoon is the season of heavy rain and wind.

So the monsoon breaks early in June, which is option D.

question: When did Christopher Marlowe get his first degree?
section:
Read the following passage and answer the questions below:

Christopher Marlowe, the son of Marlowe who is described as the clerk of St Mary's in the city of Canterbury, was born in 1564. He received his early education at The King's School in that city. He took the degrees of B.A. and M.A. in 1583 and 1587 respectively from Cambridge University. He started writing poems and became a renowned dramatist in the Admiral's Company.

Marlowe is known as one of the university wits, a group of dramatists along with Robert Greene, Thomas Nash, and George Peele. Marlowe is considered the greatest precursor to Shakespeare. When Marlowe came upon the English stage, the nature of drama was undeveloped. The verses in the dramas were lifeless. But Marlowe gave English drama an appropriate meter, diction, and method. It is really a matter of speculation what kind of greatness he would have achieved if his life had not been terminated (C++) in a duel after a brawl in a tavern (inn).

The literary life of Marlowe had a short span, from 1587 to 1593. During this period, he wrote five plays which were all tragedies as he had no comic vein. His tragedies like Dr Faustus, The Jew of Malta, and Edward Il are rated as some of the best works of the Elizabethan age. He also wrote an unfinished poem Hero and Leander and translated some parts of Ovid's (a Roman Poet) elegies.

Marlowe's subjects are mostly heroic which appeals to the imagination of the play-goers. His heroes epitomize the spirit of the Renaissance. Each of them embodies a passion and tries to achieve lies in his development of the blank verse. He put it at any cost. But Marlowe's chief contribution aside from the old rhyming lines then employed in the plays and used blank verse. Thus, the language of drama was brought closer to real life and drama was made ready for Shakespeare (1564-1616) to improve upon it. It is rightly said, "No Marlowe, no Shakespeare".
solution:
The passage says Marlowe took the degrees of B.A. and M.A. in 1583 and 1587. His first degree, the B.A., was therefore earned in 1583.

The year 1564 is his birth year, and 1587 is when he received his M.A. So option B is correct.

question: Athens had _________ the Greek-states against Persians.
section:
Use the passage to answer the questions below
Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:

The victory of the small Greek democracy of Athens over the mighty Persian Empire was furious because Athens had interceded for the other Greek city-states in revolt against Persian domination. In anger, the king sent an enormous army to defeat Athens. He thought it would take drastic steps to pacify the rebellious part of the empire.

Persia was ruled by one man. In Athens, however, all citiens helped to rule. Emboldened by this participation, Athenians were prepared to die for their city-state. Perhaps this was the secret of the remarkable victory at the marathon, the Persians tried to fool some Greek city-states by claiming to have come in peace. The frightened city of Delos refused to believe this. Not wanting to abet the conquest of Greece, they fled from their city and did not return until the Persians had left. They were wise, for the president next conquered the city of Eritrea and captured its people.

Tiny Athens stood alone against Persia. The Athenian people to their sanctuaries. There they prayed for deliverance. They asked their gods to expedite their victory. The Athenians refurbished their weapons and moved to the plan of Marathon where their little band would meet the Persians. At the last moment, soldiers from Plataea reinforced the Athenian troops.

The Athenian army attacked and Greek citizens fought bravely. The power of the mighty Persians was offset by the love that the Athenians had for their city. Athenians defeated the Persians in both archery and combat. Greek soldiers seized Persian sheep and burned them and the Persians fled in terror. Herodotus, a famous historian, reports that 6400 Persians died, compared to only 192 Athenians.
solution:
The correct answer is C — intervened on behalf.

From the passage, it is clear that Athens had interceded for the other Greek city-states against the Persian domination. This means that Athens had intervened on behalf of the other Greek city-states. Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

question: From the passage, it can be inferred that

option.a: Climate and weathering are not related
option.b: Climate determines the type of weathering
option.c: Weathering can only occur where the temperature is cool and water is available
option.d: Weathering is possible only in a place where the temperature is hot

section:
Read the passage below and answer each questions that follow:

Weathering, which is the gradual breaking down or disintegration of rocks into smaller particles or fragments by either physical or chemical process, can be affected by many factors. Generally speaking, the climatic condition of a particular area has a great effect on the weathering. Physical or mechanical weathering needs temperature and water.

Chemical weathering, on the other hand, thrives where the climate is hot. We were all taught all these in the four walls of the classroom. I made a visit to my village to see these scientific discoveries. I noticed big trees with their roots penetrating into rocks and breaking them. I initially wondered and puzzled seeing trees growing from the rock.

A similar thing happened to the soil sampling surrounding where there were rocks. I could see the rock particles mixing up with the rest of the soil.
solution:
The correct answer is B — Climate determines the type of weathering.

The passage explains that the type of weathering depends on climatic conditions: physical or mechanical weathering occurs with temperature and water, while chemical weathering thrives in hot climates.

question: From Ummi's narration, what exactly is the "Note of Salvation"?

question: One of the first things a child notices in birds is
section:
Read the passage carefully and answer the question that follows.

Birds are found almost everywhere, even in the hearts of the cities and because they are active creatures, they easily lend themselves to study. One of the first things that a child notices is how noisy many kinds of birds are. The guinea fowls are renowned for this. Even while they are feeding, many birds make characteristic calls, and with practice you can tell which species are in a wood just from these calls without seeing the birds at all. Clearly this continuous chatting is important to birds. When flocks of finches are looking for insects or seeds on the branches of trees, they could easily become separated and these calls must help keep the birds together.

There are many other occasions when birds utter calls. For example, at the sight of a bird of prey, a small bird will give its flying predator call as an alarm to other birds in the neighbourhood.

[Adapted from (1985) Objectives Test in English Comprehension, Lexis and Structure. Great Britain: William Collins Sons and co Ltd.]
solution:
The correct answer is A — noise.

The passage explicitly states, "One of the first things that a child notices is how noisy many kinds of birds are".

question: The principal was nicknamed "The Lekki Headmaster" because...

option.a: He lived in Lekki during his time as a headmaster.
option.b: He humorously imitated characters from the Village Headmaster.
option.c: He introduced a new curriculum in the school.

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba, the JAMB reading text for 2025.
solution:

Mr Bepo was nicknamed The Lekki Headmaster because of the way he used to imitate characters in the old TV drama, Village Headmaster, when he was Headmaster at Stardom Kiddies. This can be found on page 8 of the novel.

question: Which teachers were reprimanded because two of their candidates had Ds in their subjects?

option.a: Mr. Ope Wande and Mrs. Grace Apeh.
option.b: Mr. Audu and Mr. Justus Anabel.
option.c: Mr. Obong Ukake and Miss Taye Kareem.
option.d: Mr. Bepo and Mr. Ope Wande.

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba, the JAMB reading text for 2025.
solution:
The correct answer is C — Mr. Obong Ukake and Miss Taye Kareem.

The only teachers reprimanded because two candidates had Ds in their subjects were Mr. Obong Ukaku ad Miss Taye Kareem. These teachers taught Chemistry and Geography respectively. This can be found on page 8 of the novel.

question: Who among the staff at Stardom School is also a pastor?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba, the JAMB reading text for 2025.
solution:

Mr Ope Wande, the Physics teacher, is also a pastor. This can be found on page 9 of the novel.

question: What was given as a reward to teachers whose students scored distinctions in their subjects?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba, the JAMB reading text for 2025.
solution:
The correct answer is A — ₦30,000 each.

The teachers who handled subjects where candidates scored distinctions took home 30,000 each. This can be found on page 8 of the novel.

question: Why did the MD decide to send the principal home after the crying incident?

option.b: To avoid disturbing the students further.
option.c: To allow the principal to rest.

section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba, the JAMB reading text for 2025.
solution:
The correct answer is A — To protect the school’s reputation.

The MD instructed Mr Bepo to be taken home because she felt pressed to move the drama away from the school as soon as possible. She was worried about what the parents would think if they learned that the principal was weeping like a child. This can be found on page 9 of the novel.

question: Who accompanied the principal to his home on the day of the crying incident?
section: Answer the question based on your knowledge of the novel The Lekki Headmaster by Kabir Alabi Garba, the JAMB reading text for 2025.
solution:
The correct answer is B — The guidance counsellor.

The guidance counsellor accompanied Mr Bepo home on the day of the crying incident, as instructed by the MD. This can be found on page 9 of the novel.

question: Tom's excuses don't hold water.

option.a: The excuses are not logically sound
option.b: The excuses are acceptable by a few
option.d: The excuses explain the situation well

section: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is A — The excuses are not logically sound.

If an argument or theory "holds water," it means it is valid, logical or can stand up to scrutiny. When we say excuses "don't hold water," we mean they are inconsistent or unbelievable. They "leak" because they aren't solid enough to be true.

question: He got a job by paying hush money.

option.a: He bribed to get the job
option.b: He was induced to get the job
option.c: He paid exorbitant fee to get the job
option.d: He was paid for the job

section: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is A — He bribed to get the job.

The sentence uses the idiom "hush money," which refers to money paid to someone to prevent them from revealing potentially damaging or illegal information. It means that he bribed to get the job.

question: The chairman of the association tells his members not to throw in the towel.

option.b: They are not to give up
option.c: They should be ready for a trip

section: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — They are not to give up.

To "throw in the towel" is a common idiom meaning to admit defeat or to stop trying to do something because you know you cannot succeed. This phrase comes from boxing; when a fighter's coach sees their athlete is too injured or exhausted to continue, they literally throw a towel into the ring to signal a forfeit.

question: Despite his wealth, Mr Oluboye is known for tightening his belt.

option.b: He is very careful with his spending
option.c: He refuses to wear a belt at all

section: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — He is very careful with his spending.

To "tighten one's belt" is an idiom that means to live more frugally or spend less money than usual

question: The students felt the lecture was a load of crap.

option.a: The students believe the lecture was too long
option.b: The students refused to listen to the lecturer
option.c: The students thought the lecture was stupid
option.d: The students did not attend the lecture

section: Choose the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — The students thought the lecture was stupid.

"A load of crap" is a vulgar slang idiom used to describe something that is perceived as nonsense or of very poor quality.

question: Musa vehemently opposed his son's political ambition.
section: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is C — coldly.

"Vehemently" means doing something with great force, passion or intense feeling. While "vehemently" implies heat and passion, "coldly" implies a lack of emotion, passion or intensity, making it the most appropriate antonym in this context.

question: The natives were allowed to stay.
section: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is B — foreigners.

"Natives" refers to people born in a specified place or associated with a place by birth. The opposite is "foreigners," which refers to people who come from a different country or place.

question: The scientist conducted a meticulous experiment.
section: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is A — careless.

Meticulous" means showing great attention to detail and being very careful. The direct opposite is "careless," which implies a lack of attention or thought.

question: In the past, anyone who angered the gods would be killed.
section: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is B — appeased.

To "anger" someone is to make them feel strong displeasure or hostility. The most direct opposite is to "please" someone, meaning to give them pleasure or satisfaction. However, in a context that relates to the gods, "appeased" is the better answer. Action is taken (like a sacrifice or prayer) to specifically remove that anger and bring the gods back to a neutral or favourable state.

question: Despite their efforts at the last Nations Cup fiesta, the team was chastised by their employers.
section: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is B — honoured.

"Chastised" means to rebuke or punish severely. To be "honoured" is the opposite, as it involves giving someone public respect or an award for their efforts.

question: The students were reluctant to participate in the debate.
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is C — unwilling.

Reluctant means feeling or showing hesitation or a lack of desire to do something. Unwilling is a direct synonym, meaning not ready, eager or prepared to do something.

question: Parenting is really arduous even though enjoyable.
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is A — strenuous.

Arduous describes a task that is difficult and requires a great deal of effort or energy. Strenuous is the closest synonym, as it also means requiring or using great exertion or effort.

question: The debater made a very scurrilous remark about his opponent.
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is B — abusive.

Scurrilous refers to making or spreading scandalous claims about someone with the intention of damaging their reputation; it is characterised by coarseness or vulgarity. Abusive is the closest match as it implies harsh, insulting, or vitriolic language.

question: Giwa does odious things at times.
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is A — horrible.

Odious means extremely unpleasant, repulsive, or deserving of hatred. Horrible is a close synonym for something that is very unpleasant or shocking.

question: The building was haunted by a couple of spooks.
section: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.
solution:
The correct answer is A — ghosts.

Spooks is an informal term for ghosts or spirits. Ghosts are the soul or spirit of a dead person that appears to the living, which is the direct synonym for "spooks" in this context.

question: No sooner had Tobi left the house _____ it began to rain.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — than.

In English grammar, certain phrases are known as correlative conjunctions. They are pairs of words that always go together.

  • No sooner... than: This is the standard pair. Because "sooner" is a comparative adjective (ending in -er), it must be followed by "than," just like "faster than" or "taller than."

  • Hardly/Scarcely... when: This is a different structure often confused with the one above. If the sentence had started with "Hardly had Tobi left...," then "when" would be the correct choice.

question: What goes around _____ around.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — comes.

This is a common English proverb, and its wording is fixed. Proverbs usually follow a specific structure that doesn't change based on conversational context. The first part of the sentence uses the simple present tense (goes). The second part should also use the simple present tense (comes).

question: The boy _____ the flute for about thirty minutes.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — has been playing.

This tense is used for an action that started in the past and is still continuing into the present. The phrase "for about thirty minutes" indicates this. The structure for this tense is has/have + been + verb-ing.

question: Each of the answers ______ correct.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — is.

The word "Each" is the actual subject of the sentence, not "answers". In English, "Each" is always treated as a singular pronoun. Even though "answers" is plural, the verb must agree with "Each."

question: Each of the reports ______ been carefully reviewed by the committee
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — has.

The subject is "Each". Even though "reports" is plural, the verb must agree with the singular "Each".

The sentence structure requires an auxiliary verb to pair with "been" to form the present perfect tense. Has is the singular form

question: The ____ of armed robbery has been on the increase.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is D — incidence.

Incidence refers to the rate or frequency of something happening (e.g., crime rates). Incident refers to a single, specific event. Because the sentence mentions being "on the increase," it is talking about the frequency/rate of the crime, so "incidence" is the correct choice.

question: The doctor ____ him to take his medicine regularly.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — advised.

Advise is the verb. It is the action of giving a recommendation. Advice, the noun, is the recommendation itself. Since the doctor is performing an action in the past, the correct past-tense verb is "advised."

question: He was praised for the ______ achievement.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is B — laudable.

"Laudable" is an adjective meaning "deserving praise and commendation".

question: It is high time you _____ visiting that friend of yours.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is A — stopped.

When you use the phrases "It is time," "It is high time" or "It is about time" followed by a subject (in this case, "you"), you must use the Past Simple tense of the verb.

Even though the sentence refers to the present or future, we use the past tense to indicate that the action is overdue or should have happened already. This is known as the unreal past or the subjunctive mood.

question: Put Chioma's meat in _____ pack.
section: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — shiny new red lunch.

The standard hierarchy for adjectives in English is often remembered by the acronym OSASCOMP:

Order Category Examples from the Question
1 Opinion Shiny
2 Size (Not present)
3 Age New
4 Shape (Not present)
5 Color Red
6 Origin (Not present)
7 Material (Not present)
8 Purpose Lunch (describing the type of pack)

Putting them together gives you: "shiny new red lunch pack."

similarly

The word similarly is stressed on its first syllable: SIM-i-lar-ly.

Words ending in -ly usually keep the stress of the word they come from, and similar is stressed on the first syllable. Option C is correct.

question:
For the question, choose the most appropriate stress pattern from the options. The stressed syllables are written in capital letters.

convalescent
section: Choose the option that shows the correct stress pattern. The stressed syllable is written in capital letters.
solution:

question: They came with me to the MEETING.

option.a: Did they come to a meeting with me?
option.b: Did they arrive with me to the meeting?
option.c: Did they come with me to the party?
option.d: Who came with me to the meeting?

section: Choose the option that best explains the implication of the emphatic stress in the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — Did they come with me to the party?.

In emphatic stress questions, the sentence provided is the answer to a specific question. The stressed word (MEETING) is the "new" or "correcting" information. To emphasise "MEETING," the speaker must be correcting a different location mentioned in the question. Therefore, the question must have suggested a different place, like a party.

question: The woman was delivered of a baby BOY.

option.a: Was the girl delivered of a baby girl?
option.b: Was the woman delivered of two baby boys?
option.c: Was the woman delivered of a baby girl?
option.d: Was the girl delivered of a baby boy?

section: Choose the option that best explains the implication of the emphatic stress in the sentence.
solution:
The correct answer is C — Was the woman delivered of a baby girl?.

Since "BOY" is stressed, the speaker is correcting the gender. This would be the response if someone had mistakenly asked if it was a girl.

question: According to the writer, corruption is triggered off by
section:
There are many indicators with which to assess or measure corruption. One of them is the affluent living habit of the public official compared to his/her income. Corruption occurs when a public official expects to be induced to perform an act which that public official is ordinarily required to do by law.
Corruption can slow down development. One of the most widely discussed consequences of corruption is the distortion of governmental expenditure. This often results in public money being wasted on white elephant projects, rather than people-oriented services such as health and education. As a result, more opportunities are presented for corrupt use or diversion of funds. Raising the ethical standards of governance can lead to many benefits especially for the economic, political and social development of a country.
Fighting corruption and promoting governance is therefore crucial to developing an environment that facilitates the social, political and economic development of the people. However, while there are often general statements made about the effects of corruption on poverty and development, there is not an explicit recognition that corruption is more than just wealth misappropriation or abuse of power. Corruption impoverishes countries and deprives their citizens of good governance. It destabilizes economic system. When organized crime and other illegal activities flourish, basic public functions are eroded and the quality of life of the people is reduced. Bribery, for example is universally regarded as a crime, but it also reflects socio-economic problems that require broad-based preventive measures and the involvement of the society at large.
Another implication of global measures against corruption is making government work better by improving the economy. Finally, redesigning political and regulatory structures will reduce corruption and other anti-system players that encourage corrupt practices.
solution: The passage defines corruption as a situation in which a public officer expects to be induced before doing what the law already requires. So corruption is triggered by public officers.

question: Choose the word that best fills the gap labelled (6).
section:
Drought is a word that invokes strong emotions. This is not surprising as the (6)____ is usually accompanied by a number of unpleasant developments. These developments have (7)____ for all citizens, starting from the peasant farmers to the state and federal governments which may be plunged into emergency and crisis situation which, if not successfully (8)____ could result in social unrest.
The timeliness of the onset of the rains in various regions of the country and their adequate distribution thereafter have become (9)____ of considerable anxiety to all people. The fact, however, is that periodic reduction in the normal (10)____ of rainfall in the country is not new.
Since large areas of the country are drought prone, the consequence are (11)____. Dry spells could be very severe. There are two aspects of coping with drought. One has to do with emergency measures and the other with (12)____ measures. An immediate consequence of any drought would be famine. In addition, where whole populations are forced to abandon their lands or pastures in search of food, there are bound to be other lasting and (13)____ consequences such as distress, sales of cattle by livestock owners in order to buy food.
Government should provide farmers with agricultural inputs and ensure that they have easy access to these inputs under the relief (14)____. Emergency measures will be much more (15)____ if a mechanism is established to ensure adequate preparedness and defence against the occurrence of drought.
solution: Drought is something that happens; it is an event. The word that fits is phenomenon — an observable fact or event.

Drought is a word that invokes strong emotions. This is not surprising as the (6)____ is usually accompanied by a number of unpleasant developments. The timeliness of the onset of the rains in various regions of the country and their adequate distribution thereafter have become (9)____ of considerable anxiety to all people. The fact, however, is that periodic reduction in the normal (10)____ of rainfall in the country is not new.

question: Which of the following represents the writer's view in the passage?

option.a: Like most birds, evil thoughts fly swiftly in our minds without perching
option.b: Evil thoughts will continue to stings us likes vipers as long as there are enemies who cause offence
option.c: Like the pendulum, evil thoughts will always come to our minds no matter what we do
option.d: Evil thoughts may come but there is virtue in keeping them out

section: Like a clock with the pendulum in full swing, the mind moves as fast as time. But we ought to mind our thoughts, for if they turn to be our enemies. They will be too many for us and will drag us down to ruin. But some people may say that they cannot help having bad thought even though they sting like vipers. That may be true, but the question is do they hate them or not? We cannot keep thieves from looking in at our windows, but if we open our doors to them and receive them joyfully, we are bad as they. We cannot help the birds flying over our heads; but we may keep them from building their nests in our hair. Vain thoughts will knock at the door but we must not open to them. Though bad and evil thoughts rise in our hearts, they must not be allowed to reign. He who turns a morsel over and over in his mouth does so because he likes the flavours, and he who meditates upon evil, loves it, and is ripe to commit it. think of the devil, and he will appear, turn your thoughts towards will and your hands will soon follow. Snails leave their slime behind them, and so do vain thoughts. An arrow may fly through the air, and level no trace, but an evil thought always leaves a trail like serpent. Where there is much traffic of bad thinking, there will be much mire and dirty. Every wave of wicked thought adds something to the corruption which rots upon the shore of life. It is dreadful to think that a vile imagination. Once indulged, gets the key of our minds, and get in again very easily, whether or not we let it in, and what may follow, no one knows,. Nurse evil on the laps of thought, and it will grow into a giant. Therefore, there is wisdom in watching every day, the thoughts and imaginations of our hearts. Good thoughts are blessed guests and should be welcomed, well fed, and much sought after, but bad thoughts must fly out as swiftly as they moved in.
solution: The writer admits that evil thoughts may come, but insists that we should not welcome them. Keeping them out is the writer's view.

question: It can be deduced from the passage that

option.b: wise thoughts are more desirable than experience

section:
It is said that experience is the best teacher, but to learn consciously through wisdom may even be a better and more convenient way. T learn by experience is to learn from mistakes. It means you have burnt our fingers and now your eyes are open'. This is a tough, costly and inconvenient way to learn. Rather than leaving our learning to experience, why do we not learn consciously going out way to acquire knowledge and wisdom rather than leave our learning to chance.
Surely, we can learn from mistakes but why wait till when we make mistakes before we lean? We should give more premium to learning by wisdom than by experience.
This will involve one making up ones mind to be decisive in learning. We must decide to learn consciously and not necessarily from negative experiences. The first step is to realize that life is simply the outcome and outplay of decisions. Our life now is the sum total of our decisions and our future will be determined by our decisions. Our life now is the sum total of our decisions and our future will be determined by our decisions of today. If we decide to learn today we are not likely to make mistakes and when we do not make mistakes, experience need not be our best teacher.
To avoid making experience our best teacher will take more than a decision. We must couple our decision with a complete and -wholehearted devotion. We must be resolved, resolute and resilient in our bid to learn by wisdom and not necessarily by experience. This is crucial because situations and circumstances will want us to make a detour and leave our learning and life to chance. We must therefore be disciplined to remain with our resolve to make a clean break with experience as our best teacher. Disciplined in this regard means learning something new everyday by wisdom rather than rather than experience. It
means consciously getting better by the day in your chosen field. Discipline will demand taking advantage of every learning opportunity that comes our way. It will mean we must pay the price for learning by wisdom -invest in books, magazines, seminars and other means by which we may become wiser.
It is much easier and cheaper to learn consciously by wisdom than to learn by experience. Sometimes there are no signs or symptoms of miscarriage and pregnancy symptoms continue, and the miscarriage only (10)____ in a routine scan . About half all early miscarriages happen because of a problem in the way the genetic material from the egg and sperm have combined during (11)____ it can be difficult to find out why this has (12)____, but it is more likely to be due to random chance than to any underlying problem with either parent. Imbalances in pregnancy hormones, problems in the immune (13)____,and some serious infections are also thought to make miscarriages more likely. The risk of miscarriage (14)____ with age because the quality of eggs deteriorates . If a woman drinks too much alcohol or smokes heavily, the risk of miscarriage is higher. solution: Most miscarriages happen in the first twelve weeks of pregnancy.

question: The expression________stage and hall, as used in the passage, means the
section:
Music plays a vital role in human society. Good music provides entertainment and emotional release, and it accompanies activities ranging from dances to religious ceremonies. Music is heard everywhere; in auditoriums, homes, elevators, schools, sports arenas and on the streets. Recorded performance is a sensational innovation elevation of the twentieth century. Thanks to modern technology like compact disc (CD) digital video disc (DVD) and the MP 3 player, music can now be heard in divers places. Such places include living rooms and cars, jogging paths can also function as new kinds of concert halls where we can hear what we want as often as we want.
Live performances provide a special excitement. In a live performance artistes put themselves on the line. To avoid embarrassment, the artiste must train before hand and ensure that technical difficulties are avoided and that the listeners are actively involved. What is performed, how it sounds to the excitement of such a moment and feelings are exchanged between stage and hall.
Our response to a musical performance or an artiste is subjective and rooted in deep feelings. Even professional critics can differ strongly in their evaluations of a performance. There is no one ''Truth'' about what we hear and feel. Does the performed project a concept, an overall idea, or an emotion? Do some sections of a piece, but not others, communicate something to you? Can you figure out why? It is up to us as listeners to evaluate performances of music so that we can fully enjoy it. People listen to music in many different ways. For instance, music can be a barely perceived background as in a film or a totally absorbing experience as in a concert.
Adapted from Roger, K. (1990) An Appreciation Music: Fourth Brief Edition, McGrow-Hill Higher Education.
solution: In the passage, 'stage and hall' stand for the artist and the audience — the performer and the listeners.

question: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
section:
Political change and social transformation in the form of revolutions have radically altered the course of human civilization and history. Today, the world is witnessing political and social changes arising from the desire of people all over the globe for greater freedom and a voice in the way they are governed and a better standard of living. Pan of these struggles and processes have become more pronounced in the Third World since the end of the East-West cold War in the late 1980's, and in the face of the challenges being posed by the ongoing process of globalization.
While political and social changes may appear to be distinct phenomena, they are analytically inseparable. Political and social changes refer to alteration or transformations in human behavior, norms and politico-social institutions. Such changes are often a collective response to the need to change, or as a tacit recognition of a shift in the prevalent power relations in the society. Therefore, the coming to power of a new set of rulers, or the establishment of new structure and processes of governance broadly typifies socio-political changes.
It is important to note that changes can either be positive or negative. In most cases, political and social changes are caused by certain factors or reasons. This push people to collectively organize themselves to struggle for a change in the existing power relations. Another reason is to capture political power in the hope of making life better for the generality of the people. If politics is defined as who gels what, when and how; It then implies that political change refers to an alteration in the form of power and the identity of the group or class which controls the wields states power.
solution: The passage says the world is witnessing political and social changes; change cannot be stopped. So change is inevitable.

question: What, according to the passage is the most lethal form of malnutrition?
section:
Malnutrition is a condition that results from eating a diet in which nutrients are either not enough or are too much, so that the diet causes health problems. It is a tragedy of great magnitude because it is an accomplice to at least half of the 10.4 million child deaths each year. The most lethal form of malnutrition is protein-energy malnutrition (PEM), which occurs when the body does not get enough protein and energy from food. Other forms include vitamin and mineral deficiencies, obesity and diet-related chronic diseases. Malnutrition is not only a problem of the poor; it can also affect rich people who eat too much of the wrong kinds of food.

The first three years of a child's life are the most critical, because poor nutrition during this period can cause permanent damage to the brain and body. Governments must therefore invest in nutrition programmes, encourage breastfeeding and provide cheap, nutritious food for families.
solution: The passage names protein-energy malnutrition as the most lethal form of malnutrition.

question: Which of the following statements is true according to the passage?

option.a: Every human conduct often gives rise to curiosity
option.c: Curiosity is effective where there is no room for it

section: Curiosity is the desire to know or learn something. It is an inborn quality: human beings are naturally inquisitive from birth. A child who asks endless questions is showing curiosity. Curiosity thrives when the subject of discussion is of interest to us; we pay attention to what fascinates us. Suspicion can also stimulate inquisitiveness, because when we suspect that something is hidden, we want to find out more. When a person is absorbed in a subject, he gives it all his attention. Curiosity is therefore valuable, but it must be guided so that it does not lead us into other people's private affairs.

question: According to this passage, it gives the child great pleasure

option.a: to be helped to destroy the tower
option.c: to see his tower accidentally destroyed
option.d: for Daddy to see the tower he has built

section: In order to approach the problem of anxiety in play, let us consider the problem of anxiety in play, let us consider the activity of building and destroying a tower. Many a mother thinks that her little son is in a 'destructive stage' or even has a 'destructive personality' because after building a big, big tower, the boy cannot follow her advice to leave the tower for Daddy to see, but instead must kick it and make it collapse. The almost manic pleasure with which children watch the collapse in a second of the product of long play-labour has puzzled many, especially since the child does not appreciate it at all if his tower falls by accident or by a helpful uncle's hand. He, the builder, must destroy it himself. This game, I should think, arises from the not so distant experience of sudden falls at the very time when standing upright on wobbly legs afforded a new and fascinating perspective on existence. The child who consequently learns to make a tower 'stand up' enjoys causing the same tower to waver and collapse; in addition to the active mastery over a previously passive event, it makes one feel stronger to know that there is somebody weaker ----and towers, unlike little sister, can't cry and call, 'Mummy!'
solution: The passage says the child gets great pleasure from destroying the tower himself.

question: A suitable title for the above passage can be:

option.a: The good and the bad side of the media
option.b: The mass media and the people

section:
The term Mass Communication occurs when information is disseminated to a relatively large number of people in different places. it should be seen as the same thing with talking face to face with someone else. With mass communication, there is no answer, smile, laugh or lock of surprise. the people who receive the message are as far away from the source of the message as far away as you are from the announcers on the radio or from the newscasters on television, or from the writer of a column in the local newspaper.
There are three identifiable means of errors in mass communication. There is one done through the printed words, books, magazine and newspapers. The other is primarily radio, but also records and tape recordings. Also, it can be done through a combination of sound and pictures as in television, films and the more recently popular video tape. Together, they are referred to as the mass media.
All media can be used to inform and entertain. However, there are coverts roles played. It may be to educate as in school broadcast. Again, the aim may be to persuade as when the media are used by advertisers or for political broadcasts. The media are often in strong position to influence public opinion because they select the topics to be presented and can stress the importance of one issue over the other.
The mass media have, in recent times, come under acerbic criticism. Many presenters have become not only conscientized but also immensely concerned about the possible effects that science of violence and bad behavior may have on their children. More worrisome are the potential danger of political and commercial propaganda.
solution: The passage discusses the mass media and how they affect the people, so the best title is The mass media and the people.
